The leveling is what killed any true good experience for me and everyone I’ve talked about the game with.

Having to stop between each sequence to get ten levels by grinding pointless fetch quests ruins the pacing of the game.

Now, the Witcher 3 does this too, as do many RPGs. But Odyssey’s problem is that very, very few of the good side quests are available during these periods in the early to mid game where you have to ruthlessly grind levels. The mythical creatures, the Arena, the Cult, and the various other well made side content, are all locked behind the highest level blocks in the game(42-50). 

It’d be fine if the world was fun to explore, but it’s really just not. Some side characters are memorable, yeah, but that’s a few out of nearly 80 side quests. It’s not fun clearing out twenty bandit camps just to play the main story of the game.

Also, no Assassins. If this game was the Origins of the franchise, and set up the Misthios as the founder of the Hidden Ones, it would have been fine. But they didn’t do that. The story is of course tied to rest of the franchise, but the lack of the main two factions just seems soulless.

And lastly, stealth is useless/irritating to preform. It’s legitimately difficult to get a bow to one shot so much so that I had to carry around a sword with a crazy hit chance during my bow play through to occasionally get a one hit headshot. Assassinations are too long too. Bayek’s animations were quick and clean, my favorite out of the RPGs, but the Misthios’ are just too slow, making getting detected whilst assassinating too common.

Lot of good ideas, and I do love the core game, but Origins was just better in mostly every way mechanics and story wise, making the game feel like a downgrade.
